messages:
alex: @liaison-emi customer acme-inc reports sudden p99 spike ~2.3s and ~4% 504s starting ~10:12 UTC. They see long queue times before worker handoff. attaching quick repro and logs. :rotating_light:

alex: repro curl we used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \\ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \\ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\ 
  -d '{"model":"rwi-compat-1","input":"lorem ipsum ... repeat to blow up tokens"}'
```

alex: from customer trace (ingress logs):
```
[10:12:03] ingress admit_queue.size=842 admit_queue.p99_ms=2300 worker_free=0
[10:12:04] worker_pool.saturated=12/12 schedule_delay_ms=1200
[10:12:05] request id=xyz dropped=0 retry=1 -> long wait
```

alex: they say it started right after the recent ingress admission change rollout at ~10:05. tagging @ryan oncall

ryan: seeing the alert now, pulling dashboards. timeline makes sense. ingress admit queue depth jumped at 10:06. can someone confirm recent deploy? @deploy-bot any info?

deploy-bot: Deploy successful: git@main:feat/ingress-admit-queue (deploy #4221) finished at 10:05:18 UTC by jess.

jess: I rolled the admit-queue size heuristic change (lowered soft-cap) to reduce latency in normal load. didn't expect it to cause this ramp. investigating host metrics now.

ingress-alert-bot: [ALERT] ingress.admit_queue.depth > 600 (600 -> 842) at 10:11 UTC. p95_latency increased 400ms -> 900ms. p99_latency increased 900ms -> 2300ms.

tess: quick thought — if admit threshold got too aggressive we might be serializing more requests into a smaller working set causing KV cache thrash. can we temporarily revert or enable fallback routing to smaller model variant?

samir: I can flip the admit soft-cap back to previous value from the rollout, or we can open a hot-path bypass that sends low-size requests straight to the fast pool. Which is lower-risk?

ryan: revert config first (fast rollback) — lower blast radius. samir, can you push rollback to canary 1 now and monitor p99 for next 5m? I'll keep customer updated.

samir: pushing rollback to canary 1 -> applied at 10:13:02 UTC.

jess: adding logs from worker side showing saturation and blocked epoll syscalls. small snippet:
```
worker-17: epoll_wait blocked 1200ms repeatedly
worker-17: kvcache.misses increased 4x after admit change
```

ryan: good data. liaison-emi please tell acme we'll do a config rollback and investigate root cause; ask them if they can preserve a sample request id for us.

liaison-emi: told customer rollback in progress, they provided sample request id xyz and a short trace. they want ETA ~15-30m, escalation to engineering accepted.

samir: canary rollback completed to 100% at 10:15:20 UTC. watching metrics now.

ingress-alert-bot: [NOTICE] ingress.admit_queue.depth decreased 842 -> 120 over 2m. p95_latency trending down to 220ms, p99 to 300ms.

alex: customer confirmed latency back to normal on their side. they still want a postmortem and a mitigation plan so this doesn't reoccur.

tess: follow-ups to include:
- stricter rollout guard for admit heuristic (require load-sim and tail-latency test)
- auto-fallback routing to smaller quantized model on queue buildup
- alert runbook update: auto-rollback if p99 > 1000ms for >2m after config change
- improve KV cache metrics visibility in ingress dashboards

jess: I'll open a PR with the rollout-gate changes and add a canary monitor.

ryan: good. logging action items here and assigning owners. customer updated. closing thread once PR merged and runbook updated. :white_check_mark:
